AI translation: on-device detection/OCR/text-removal + cloud LLM

Yakuyomi can detect, OCR, erase and re-typeset speech bubbles for you. Everything except the translation itself runs on this device — your images never leave it. Only the recognised text is sent to the cloud LLM you choose (your own API key — this can cost money).\n\nTranslation is off by default. Set it up now, or any time under Settings → Translation.
A bottom search ball for the library and browse
Browse a source offline; a background crawl catches up to where you left off
See how much you have translated and read
How to set up and use translation

Detection, OCR and text removal all run on your phone. Only the OCR\'d text goes to the LLM provider you pick — using your own API key and endpoint. Your images, and the detection / OCR / erase steps, never leave the device. There is no analytics or telemetry.\n\nCloud translation may cost money, billed by your provider. Tapping Got it at the end means you understand this.

1. Pick a provider and paste your API key.
Settings → Translation → Provider. Default is DeepSeek; OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, Qwen, OpenRouter and self-hosted (Sakura / custom) also work. Paste the key from your provider's dashboard — it is encrypted on this device. For a self-hosted or custom provider, also fill in the API base.

2. Get the models (detector, OCR, text-removal).
Settings → Translation → Models → Download models (about 96 MB, verified). Or bring your own: drop the model files into the models folder in your storage location. The Model status row shows a check or cross for each.

3. Pick your languages.
Default is Japanese → Traditional Chinese (Taiwan). Change the target or source any time.

Translate on download — turn on Translate chapters on download. Every chapter you download is then translated automatically in the background, and the page images are replaced in place. Best when you download ahead and read later.

Live (read-as-you-go) — turn on Live translation, a separate switch. When you open an unread chapter it is translated in the background and pages swap in as they become ready (a Translating X/Y pill shows at the top-left). Opening an undownloaded chapter downloads it first, then translates. Use Live translation categories to limit it to, or exclude, certain library categories.

The two switches are independent: use either, both, or neither.
By hand, and keeping it tidy

Manual translate — on a manga's chapter list, downloaded chapters show a translate button. The icon spins while running, turns the accent colour when done, and red on error. Long-press to multi-select, then tap Translate in the bottom bar.

Translation queue — More → Translation queue lists everything in progress with its status. Pause or resume, cancel, or retry failed chapters there.

Re-render — already translated a chapter but want cleaner text removal? Change the method in Settings (you will be asked to update existing chapters), or long-press a page → Re-render. No re-OCR or re-translation needed.
A prompt hint; leave blank to let the LLM infer. The actual source is decided by the OCR model (BYOM).
